scope_statement: Survey theoretical models explaining platform growth, network effects, governance, monetization, and competition mechanisms listed.
must_cover: Two- and multi-sided market structures and intermediation value creation
Direct and indirect network externalities, positive and negative effects
Critical mass, tipping points, and the chicken–egg dilemma in growth
Multi-homing, single-homing, and switching costs affecting retention
Platform governance: rules, rankings, access, and quality control
Monetization and price structures including fees and commissions
Competition dynamics: winner-takes-most versus multi-platform coexistence
should_cover: Formal models and dynamic growth path analyses
Empirical measures and identification of network effects
Mechanisms linking pricing to network externalities
Design and effects of ranking and matching algorithms
Policy-relevant implications within listed theoretical concepts
must_avoid: Additional market or organizational theories beyond listed concepts
Firm-level organizational theory and management strategy literature
Broad macroeconomic or non-platform market theories
main_query: platform network effects multi-sided markets governance monetization multi-homing competition
facet_queries: direct and indirect network externalities positive negative
critical mass tipping points chicken-egg dilemma
multi-homing switching costs market share effects
platform governance rules rankings access control
monetization pricing fees commissions network effects
formal growth-path and dynamic tipping models
matching algorithms and quality control mechanisms
measurement of platform scale and engagement
scoring_guidance: Prioritize sources explicitly addressing the listed concepts; favor formal models and empirical identification of network effects. Moderate preference for seminal and recent high-quality studies. Penalize works focused on broader organizational or general market theories outside scope.
